title: Linear equations involving brackets
competency: Define a linear equation and solve linear equations, including ones with brackets.

keywords.def: Two algebraic expressions joined by an equal sign (=).
An equation that can be written ax + b = 0 with a ≠ 0. The highest exponent of x is 1.
Add, subtract, multiply or divide both sides by the same number (not 0 for × and ÷).
The value of the variable that makes the equation true.
a(b + c) = ab + ac. Multiply each term in the bracket.

en.text: An equation joins two expressions with an equal sign, like 3x − 1 = 6. A linear equation has the variable only to the power 1, like x + 3 = 2x − 1. 2x² + 3 = 2x − 1 is not linear. The left part is the L.H.S, the right part the R.H.S.

screens.title: A level balance
screens.ask: A balance is level. One pan has a box x. The other has 10 kg. What is x?
screens.after: The balance is level, so both sides weigh the same: x = 10 kg. An equation is like a level balance.

screens.title: Definitions 3.9 and 3.10
paras: Two different algebraic expressions joined by an equal sign (=) make an equation.
A linear equation in x can be written as ax + b = 0, where a ≠ 0.
In a linear equation the highest exponent of the variable is one.

screens.title: Example 1 and Example 2
paras: In 3x + 5 = x − 1, the L.H.S is 3x + 5 and the R.H.S is x − 1.
screens.note: L.H.S = left-hand side. R.H.S = right-hand side.

screens.title: When are both sides equal?
screens.note: Move x. The two sides are equal only when x = −3. Then both sides are −4, like a level balance.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Two algebraic expressions joined by an equal sign (=).
An equation that can be written ax + b = 0 with a ≠ 0. The highest exponent of x is 1.

screens.text: Equations: which one of these is an equation?
screens.why:
An equation has an equal sign (=).
2 + x has no = sign: it is an expression.
x > 2 uses >, not =.
Only x = 2 is an equation.

A linear equation needs an = sign.
The highest power of x must be 1.
x − 1 = 5, 3x = 0 and x − 3 + 4x = 2x − 2 are linear.
2y − 2 and x > 0 have no = sign.
2x² = 4 has x², so it is not linear.
screens.clue: Is there an = sign? Is there an x² or x³?
screens.text: Sort each one: is it a linear equation?
Sides of an equation: in 3x + 5 = x − 1, what is the R.H.S?
screens.why:
R.H.S means right-hand side.
It is everything to the right of the = sign.
In 3x + 5 = x − 1, that is x − 1.
3x + 5 is the L.H.S.

screens.text: Simplify, then decide: which one is a linear equation?
screens.why:
x² + 3x = x² + 6: subtract x² from both sides.
This leaves 3x = 6, which is linear.
x(x + 1) = 5 is x² + x = 5: not linear.
2x² = 8 has x². x > 4 has no = sign.
screens.clue: Simplify each one first. Does an x² cancel?

en.text: An equation stays true if you do the same thing to both sides. You may add or subtract the same number. You may multiply or divide by the same number that is not 0. For x − 10 = 6, add 10 to both sides: x = 16.

screens.title: Add to both pans
screens.ask: A balance has 6 kg on each pan. You add 4 kg to both pans. What happens?
screens.after: Adding the same weight to both sides keeps it level. Equations work the same way.

screens.title: Rules of transforming equations
screens.ask: If a = b, what can you do to both sides? Tap each rule.
items: If a = b, then a + c = b + c.
If a = b, then a − c = b − c.
If a = b, then a × c = b × c.
If a = b, then a/c = b/c.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Add, subtract, multiply or divide both sides by the same number (not 0 for × and ÷).

screens.text: Name the rule: 2x − 4 = 6 becomes 2x = 10. What was done?
screens.why:
We want to remove the −4.
Add 4 to both sides: 2x − 4 + 4 = 6 + 4.
This gives 2x = 10.
This is Rule 1: add the same number to both sides.

y is multiplied by 8.
Divide both sides by 8 (Rule 4).
y = 72 ÷ 8 = 9.
Check: 8 × 9 = 72.

screens.ask: Solve the equation: 20 − x = 15. So x = ___
screens.why:
Subtract 20 from both sides: −x = 15 − 20.
So −x = −5.
Divide both sides by −1: x = 5.
Check: 20 − 5 = 15.

Multiply both sides by 5: 2x = 50.
Divide both sides by 2: x = 25.
Check: 2 × 25 = 50, and 50 ÷ 5 = 10.
screens.clue: Multiply by 5 first, then divide by 2.

screens.why:
Multiply both sides by 4: 3x = −24.
Divide both sides by 3: x = −8.
Check: 3 × (−8) = −24, and −24 ÷ 4 = −6.
screens.clue: Clear the 4 first, then the 3. Watch the sign.

en.text: Shifting a term to the other side changes its sign. In x − 5 = 10, −5 moves across as +5, so x = 15. Put the variable terms on one side and the numbers on the other. Then check by putting the answer back.

screens.title: Moving across
screens.ask: x − 5 = 10. If you move −5 to the other side, what does it become?
screens.after: Moving a term across the = sign changes its sign: x = 10 + 5 = 15.

screens.title: Shifting terms
paras: Solving x − 5 = 10, you add 5 to both sides and get x = 10 + 5.
This is the same as shifting −5 to the other side. It becomes +5.
When you shift a term to the other side, its sign changes.
screens.note: Collect the variable terms on one side and the numbers on the other.

screens.title: Solve 5x − 10 = 6 − 3x
steps: Shift −3x to the left (it becomes +3x) and −10 to the right (it becomes +10).

screens.title: Check 5x − 10 = 6 − 3x
screens.note: Move x. Only x = 2 makes both sides equal (both are 0).

screens.title: Key words
defs: The value of the variable that makes the equation true.

screens.why:
Shift x to the left: it becomes −x.
2x − x = 4.
So x = 4.
Check: 2(4) = 8 and 4 + 4 = 8.
screens.clue: Get all the x terms on the left.

screens.why:
Shift 2x to the left and +5 to the right.
8x − 2x = 17 − 5.
6x = 12.
Divide by 6: x = 2.
Check: 8(2) + 5 = 21 and 2(2) + 17 = 21.

Shift 4x to the left and −9 to the right.
3x − 4x = 5 + 9.
−x = 14.
Divide by −1: x = −14.
Check: 3(−14) − 9 = −51 and 4(−14) + 5 = −51.
screens.clue: After shifting you get −x. Divide by −1.

screens.why:
Simplify the right side: 5 + 17 = 22.
So 12x + 7 = 22 − 3x.
Shift: 12x + 3x = 22 − 7.
15x = 15, so x = 1.
Check: 12 + 7 = 19 and 5 − 3 + 17 = 19.

screens.text: Spot the mistake. Dawit solved 4x − 3 = x + 9 like this: 4x − x = 9 − 3, so 3x = 6 and x = 2. Is he right?
screens.why:
Check x = 2: 4(2) − 3 = 5, but 2 + 9 = 11. Not equal.
His mistake: −3 moved across but kept its sign.
It should become +3: 4x − x = 9 + 3.
3x = 12, so x = 4.
Check: 4(4) − 3 = 13 and 4 + 9 = 13.
screens.clue: Check his answer: is 4(2) − 3 equal to 2 + 9?

en.text: To solve an equation with brackets, first remove the brackets with the distributive property. Then collect variable terms on one side and numbers on the other. For 4(2x + 3) = 36: 8x + 12 = 36, 8x = 24, x = 3.

screens.title: First step
screens.after: Remove the bracket first: 3x + 6 = 0. Then 3x = −6 and x = −2.

screens.title: To solve linear equations involving brackets
paras: 1. Remove the brackets using the distributive property.
2. Collect variable terms on one side and constants on the other. Change the sign when you shift a term.
table: For any numbers a, b, c

screens.title: Bracket rules with numbers
screens.ask: Tap each rule. The numbers show it works.

screens.title: Key words
defs: a(b + c) = ab + ac. Multiply each term in the bracket.

screens.why:
Remove the bracket: 3x + 6 = 0.
Shift +6: 3x = −6.
Divide by 3: x = −2.
Check: 3(−2 + 2) = 3 × 0 = 0.

A minus in front means multiply each term by −1.
(−1) × (−2x) = +2x.
(−1) × 9 = −9.
Answer: 2x − 9.
screens.clue: A minus in front changes every sign inside.

screens.ask: Solve the equation with brackets: 8(2y − 6) = 5(3y − 7). So y = ___
Solve the equation with brackets: 3 − 2(2x + 1) = x − 14. So x = ___
screens.why:
Remove the bracket: 3 − 4x − 2 = x − 14.
Simplify: 1 − 4x = x − 14.
Shift: −4x − x = −14 − 1, so −5x = −15.
Divide by −5: x = 3.
Check: 3 − 2(7) = −11 and 3 − 14 = −11.

screens.ask: Solve the equation with brackets: 2(x + 3) − (x − 4) = 15. So x = ___
screens.why:
Remove the brackets: 2x + 6 − x + 4 = 15.
Combine: x + 10 = 15.
Shift +10: x = 5.
Check: 2(8) − (1) = 16 − 1 = 15.

math.integer-signs.name: Signs when multiplying and adding integers

screens.title: Integer signs
steps: Adding different signs: −5 + 3 = −2 (take 3 from 5, keep the sign of 5).

screens.why:
Both numbers are negative: the signs are the same.
Same signs give a positive answer.
3 × 4 = 12.
So (−3) × (−4) = 12. (−12 would need different signs.)
screens.clue: Are the signs the same or different?

items.text: Linear or not? Is 2x² = 4 a linear equation?
items.why:
A linear equation has x with highest power 1.
Here x has power 2 (x²).
So 2x² = 4 is not linear. No.
items.clue: Look at the power of x.

items.text: Linear or not? Is x − 3 + 4x = 2x − 2 a linear equation?
items.why:
It has an = sign.
Every x has power 1.
It simplifies to 5x − 3 = 2x − 2.
So it is linear. Yes.
items.clue: Look at the powers of x.

items.text: Name the rule: x + 1 = 2 becomes x = 1 by:
items.why:
We want to remove the +1.
Subtract 1 from both sides: x + 1 − 1 = 2 − 1.
This gives x = 1 (Rule 2).

We want to clear the /3.
Multiply both sides by 3: 3 × 2x/3 = 5 × 3.
This gives 2x = 15 (Rule 3).

x is multiplied by −8.
Divide both sides by −8: x = 12 ÷ (−8).
Different signs give a negative: x = −12/8.
Simplify: x = −3/2 = −1.5.
Check: −8 × (−1.5) = 12.

Multiply both sides by 5: 2x = 50.
Divide by 2: x = 25.
Check: 2(25)/5 = 50/5 = 10.

items.ask: Solve the equation: 20 − x = 15. So x = ___
items.why:
Subtract 20 from both sides: −x = −5.
Divide by −1: x = 5.
Check: 20 − 5 = 15.

Add 4 to both sides: 2x = 20.
Divide by 2: x = 10.
Check: 2(10) − 4 = 16.

Shift 4x to the left and −9 to the right.
3x − 4x = 5 + 9, so −x = 14.
Divide by −1: x = −14.
Check: −42 − 9 = −51 and −56 + 5 = −51.

Combine like terms: 5x − 4x = x.
So x − 3 = 13.
Shift −3: x = 13 + 3 = 16.
Check: 80 − 3 − 64 = 13.

Shift x to the left and 3 to the right.
−x − x = 9 − 3, so −2x = 6.
Divide by −2: x = −3.
Check: 3 + 3 = 6 and −3 + 9 = 6.

Shift −x to the left and −9 to the right.
3x + x = 19 + 9, so 4x = 28.
Divide by 4: x = 7.
Check: 21 − 9 = 12 and −7 + 19 = 12.

Combine: 3x + 2x = 5x, so 10 = 5x − 5.
Shift −5: 10 + 5 = 5x, so 15 = 5x.
Divide by 5: x = 3.
Check: 9 − 5 + 6 = 10.

items.ask: Solve the equation: x − 5 = 2x + 13 + x. x = ___
items.why:
Combine the right side: 2x + x = 3x.
So x − 5 = 3x + 13.
Shift: x − 3x = 13 + 5, so −2x = 18.
Divide by −2: x = −9.
Check: −9 − 5 = −14 and −18 + 13 − 9 = −14.

Nothing multiplies the bracket, so just remove it: x − 1 = 11.
Shift −1: x = 11 + 1.
x = 12.
Check: 12 − 1 = 11.

items.ask: Solve the equation with brackets: 6(8y + 3) = 4(7y + 5). y = ___
Solve the equation with brackets: 7 − (x + 1) = 9 − (2x − 1). x = ___
items.why:
Left side: 7 − x − 1 = 6 − x.
Right side: 9 − 2x + 1 = 10 − 2x.
So 6 − x = 10 − 2x.
Shift: −x + 2x = 10 − 6, so x = 4.
Check: 7 − 5 = 2 and 9 − 7 = 2.

items.ask: Solve the equation with brackets: 5(1 − 2a) − 3(4 − 4a) = 0. a = ___
items.why:
Remove the brackets: 5 − 10a − 12 + 12a = 0.
Combine: 2a − 7 = 0.
Shift −7: 2a = 7.
Divide by 2: a = 7/2 = 3.5.
Check: 5(−6) − 3(−10) = −30 + 30 = 0.

items.ask: Solve the equation with brackets: 3x + 7 + 3(x − 1) = 2(2x + 6). x = ___
items.why:
Remove the brackets: 3x + 7 + 3x − 3 = 4x + 12.
Combine: 6x + 4 = 4x + 12.
Shift: 6x − 4x = 12 − 4, so 2x = 8.
x = 4.
Check: 12 + 7 + 9 = 28 and 2(14) = 28.

items.ask: Solve the equation with brackets: 5(2x + 1) + 3(3x − 4) = 4(5x − 6). x = ___
Solve for x: m(x − 1) = 0, where m ≠ 0. x = ___
items.why:
Remove the bracket: mx − m = 0.
Shift −m: mx = m.
Divide both sides by m (m ≠ 0): x = 1.
Check: m(1 − 1) = m × 0 = 0.

items.ask: Solve for x: m(x + n) = mn, where m ≠ 0. x = ___
items.why:
Remove the bracket: mx + mn = mn.
Shift mn: mx = mn − mn = 0.
Divide by m (m ≠ 0): x = 0.
Check: m(0 + n) = mn.

test.text: Linear or not: which one is a linear equation?
test.why:
Linear means the highest power of x is 1.
x + 3 = 2x − 1: x has power 1. Linear.
x = 2x³ − 6 has x³. 2x² + 3 = 7 has x².
So the answer is x + 3 = 2x − 1.

Subtract 4 from both sides: x = −6 − 4.
x = −10.
Check: −10 + 4 = −6.

Add 8 to both sides: 2x = 12.
Divide by 2: x = 6.
Check: 2(6) − 8 = 4.
